steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund... wait, Raimund!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What are you doing?!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Taking you away from here.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I know what's going on. I won't let them take you!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: No need to be scared. Come with me. We'll help you—

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: N-No! I'm not scared!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund! Let me go... you don't get it!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Sorry... was I hurting you?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'm okay.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I-I decided to go with them to Laterano, Raimund.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What are you saying? Did they threaten you? You'll die if you go there!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I deserve to!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Let me go, Raimund. No one threatened me. I killed Fina. I can't run away from this!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Delfina...? That was an accident...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: No! I don't want to hear that anymore, especially from you!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: An accident... an accident! Of course I wouldn't point a gun at Fina on purpose. It was a tragic accident... but she's dead! Dead!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: She'll never open her eyes again. She'll never speak to us again!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Fortuna, calm down... you'll hurt yourself!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I want to calm down... I don't want to be crying like this!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But why doesn't anyone blame me? Why does everyone call it an accident? As though that means Fina's death didn't matter?!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I killed Fina! What difference does it make that it was an accident?!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Breathe. Don't hold it in.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huff... hah...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huff...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Feeling better?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'm sorry, Raimund. I shouldn't be like this, but I don't know what to do...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I only know that I can't go. I can't run away and pretend nothing happened. I can't accept that it was an accident.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: This is my sin...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: No more talking.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Don't worry about me, Raimund. It might not be that bad.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Serpilia, that Lateran emissary who came today, she was kind to me. I wasn't mistreated.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Maybe they'll lock me up when we get to Laterano.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I have horns now... I don't know if I'm Sankta anymore. It doesn't really matter if I'm not...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Anyway, I'm fine, Raimund. You—

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I can't let it happen.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I can't just leave you like this, Fortuna—

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund? What are you...?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: (Hush! Hold your breath...)

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: (Someone's coming!)

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: He hung up.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: When did you get Richele over to your side?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: That's an exaggeration. He's always been that type who only does what's good for him.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: He's even better than I am at looking out for himself...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I feel like I'm being watched...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Has your paranoia finally caused you to hallucinate, Oren?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'd rather believe that there really is someone watching in the shadows.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Just a joke. Don't look at me like that.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Where's the fallen angel you were watching?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Sound asleep, I would think.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Stay on topic.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What were you saying about pushing the schedule forward? Not that you can't, but that's not what we agreed on.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Why the sudden change? Give me a reason.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What difference does it make to you?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Not much, which is why I can choose not to cooperate.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Unless my memory deceives me, I have command of the troops.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'm prepared to write a report.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You're anxious, Oren. What's the matter?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: This is a secret operation. It's not so easy to deploy troops, if the matter of the saints didn't catch His Holiness's attention.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Even then, His Holiness seems to have noticed something, and specifically sent Federico... you know how hard it is to pull wool over Federico's eyes.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Do you really think you succeeded?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Probably not.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: But I would say I know him well enough. There won't be much trouble if he doesn't pursue the matter. Our goal is just to stop everyone who wants to leave, isn't it?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: On the other hand, the beast is out of the bag the moment you give the order to attack.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Federico isn't concerned about the means, only the end.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh, you think so?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Let me just make it clear that if you get on his bad side, I can't stop him.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: So much for camaraderie.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: A message? Who could it be at this hour...? Oh.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: See for yourself.

a.text: Bring Oren to the narthex immediately.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So much for the wool.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Everything you talked about, I'll take care of. Do as I say.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: We take control of the abbey immediately. Get all available hands on it.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: ...That urgent?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: An old man has given the last sixty years of his life to the abbey. He went so far as to imprison Lateran emissaries for the sake of those Sarkaz.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: He suddenly became open to compromise in desperate circumstances, even proposing something so ritualistic as a final farewell... why do you think?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: That, plus some Sarkaz who are not entirely unknown, and 'visitors' hiding in the shadows...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: We have to act quickly.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I've got a bad feeling...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Take control? What does he mean... why?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Don't you understand? The Sankta lied to us!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I have to tell Gerald! I knew it! Those Laterans never intended to play nice.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: The situation has changed. It's dangerous for you to be with me. Find a safe place; I doubt they'll do anything to you immediately—

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Wait, Raimund!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: *deep breath*

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I changed my mind. I'm coming with you.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: My, my, what a coincidence to run into you two!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'm so glad you're safe, Lemuen.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Any news?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You look concerned, Executor Richele.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I found something that I thought warranted investigation. It has to do with the abbot, but... anyway, more investigation is needed.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What about you, Federico? What are you doing?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Work.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Um, ok, that much is obvious... what did you find? Something to do with the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I heard last night's fire was started by angry Sarkaz. Is that true?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What's this? Rehearsing your stand-up comedy routine?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Enough jokes.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Jokes?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Oren and Serpilia will be here soon.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Well, by the sound of it, you knew Oren hid on purpose from the get-go?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Obviously.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: That's just his luck, isn't it? He just can't seem to get away from you, whether at the Summit of Nations or now.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I allowed Oren to act of his own accord, because the complicated situation at the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii called for a Plan B.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But maybe he needs a reminder...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So, what's going on? I was told to come immediately and bring Oren.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Ah, there you are, Oren. Finally decided to show your face?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: It's been a while, Lemuen.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Can't you be a little nicer to me? We're partners on this mission, after all.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's because we're partners that you're still able to talk.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Whatever your plan was, the situation here doesn't call for that kind of aggression. It's time to stop, Oren.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Couldn't you two pretend you didn't see anything, like that guy over there?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Oh, er, I would prefer if you didn't drag me into this...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will deal with Richele when we return to the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Gratias, Oren.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As for you, Oren.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you truly believe there is a need for you to operate independently, you may try to persuade me.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Well, since there's no one else here, I'll cut straight to the chase.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Did you really think I wouldn't notice that you were trying to let those two kids go?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: A fallen Sankta and a Sarkaz. Even a blind man would notice.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I've been patient for far too long.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Are you criticizing my methods?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Not at all, not at all.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: But I have my own methods. We've wasted too much time here. It's we need to consider how to can get this done quickly, with no loose ends.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And so you decided to deploy a special forces unit?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You make it sound so easy. You know full well that deploying troops and giving the order are two different things.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Do you know how hard it was to come up with a justification that even His Holiness could not rebuke?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Now, I have one.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: That Sarkaz boy—Raimund? Arson of a sacrarium is a serious offense, that's before I mention that he's Sarkaz. We're perfectly justified in seizing him and taking the investigation into our hands.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He was not the one who set fire to the sacrarium. Your justification is baseless.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have no need of your intervention until I uncover the truth.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The truth? Ha. Is the truth really important?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What is more rational and logical than taking control and securing order?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Did you not consider it, Federico? Is the truth really so important to you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Did you not consider the possibility of the locals resisting, Oren?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I didn't think you'd say something so silly, Lemuen. If the Sarkaz want to resist...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: So much the better.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Who's there?!
The sound of knocking echoes through the hall.
The door creaks open, and the unusually bright rays of the moon pour in through the gap.
There is a figure standing in the moonlight.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Senior Federico...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clément?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I finally found you, Senior Federico.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I was asked to bring you this...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: By whom? What is—
The rest of the sentence vanishes into the night.
The tall and thin figure approaches, his back to the moonlight, his head bowed.
It is as if all the light in the room had converged upon him, but the overly bright light also casts a dark, suffocating shadow.
Now, Federico sees what Clément is holding.
What he said he was asked to bring to Federico.
A dagger.
Old, but no less sharp for it, once hidden in the belt of a certain someone.
Next to the dagger...
There is a package wrapped in cloth that has been dyed a deep shade of red, from which some sort of liquid continues to drip.
What is it?
It is...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The sinner, Holst Tyfindale, offers his head freely.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The sinner had admitted responsibility for all the crimes, all the evils committed hitherto.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: He has now paid his price. All that remains is a band of insignificant vagrants.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Will the reverend emissaries of Laterano show grace and mercy?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Senior Federico... I bring you Gerald's last words.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: He begs you take the head of the fugitive Holst and his weapon...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: In exchange, spare Fortuna and Raimund...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Spare the other Sarkaz.
